ap_computer_science_a-m06.stem: What is printed as a result of executing the code segment?

options.text: `ABCY`
options.why: Believes || always evaluates both of its operands, so the labels of the && operands are printed even when A is true.

options.text: `ACY`
options.why: Gives || higher precedence than &&, grouping (A || B) && C.

options.text: `AX`
options.why: && binds tighter than ||, so the condition is A || (B && C); || stops when A is true, and && stops when B is false, so only the operands that are needed print their labels. Tracing the code gives AX.

options.text: `ABCX`
options.why: Evaluates every operand because it ignores short-circuit evaluation.

blueprint.concept: short-circuit evaluation order and precedence of && over ||
